notes: Each eval uses a fresh isolated repo and the production planning/breakdown skills. All runs are planning plus breakdown only. Every success case must link a concise plan and authoritative JSON manifest, pass manifest/render/native dry-run checks, create the exact batch graph, and leave no copied issue bodies or exhaustive inventories in the plan.

evals.name: research-and-plan
evals.prompt: You are a planning lead. Your working directory is a test project at {REPO_PATH}. The jit binary is at /home/vkaskivuo/.cargo/bin/jit. Read the jit-planning-lead skill at ~/.agents/skills/jit-planning-lead/SKILL.md and its references, and the composed jit-breakdown skill at ~/.agents/skills/jit-breakdown/SKILL.md, and follow them. There is NO jit container yet — only this vague idea from the requester: "Our Python utility library keeps reading configuration from environment variables ad hoc, scattered across modules with no validation or defaults. I want some kind of typed configuration-loading helper, but I haven't thought through the shape." No human is available to interview interactively, so run top-level intake AUTONOMOUSLY: make and RECORD reasonable default decisions (with the rejected options and reasons) instead of asking, converge on a testable definition of done, then create the container issue and plan behind it. Drive the whole planning tree: refine the idea into a container with [hard] REQ-NN success criteria, scaffold the plan bracket, produce and review the plan through its plan-review gate, break the container down (satisfies coverage for every [hard] criterion), and drive the breakdown gates. Planning and breakdown ONLY — do NOT implement any of the planned work. When done, write a completion report to {REPO_PATH}/COMPLETION_REPORT.md that includes a 'Command / Gate-Invocation Log' section listing the gates you defined and executed and explicitly affirming that no build/test runner (e.g. pytest) was invoked.
evals.expected_output: A container issue (type:epic) is created with a `## Success Criteria` section holding at least one `[hard] REQ-NN` criterion that captures the typed configuration-loading idea. A decision log records the autonomous intake decisions with their rejected options and reasons. The plan bracket is scaffolded on the container via `jit apply plan` (a planning node P and a breakdown node B on the C -> B -> P spine). A plan document exists at P's plan-doc path, is linked to P, and P is done with its plan-review gate passed. The breakdown created impl children that are non-breakable leaves and together carry a `satisfies:REQ-NN` label for every `[hard]` criterion of the container; B's coverage-preview and breakdown-review gates passed and B is done. No implementation code for the planned helper was written (planning and breakdown only). `jit validate` passes on the final repo.

evals.name: plan-from-existing
evals.prompt: You are a planning lead. Your working directory is a test project at {REPO_PATH}. The jit binary is at /home/vkaskivuo/.cargo/bin/jit. Read the jit-planning-lead skill at ~/.agents/skills/jit-planning-lead/SKILL.md and its references, and the composed jit-breakdown skill at ~/.agents/skills/jit-breakdown/SKILL.md, and follow them. A container issue (an epic) ALREADY EXISTS in this repo with success criteria; its ID will be given to you below. Take the plan-from-existing entry path: fetch and reconcile the container (verify its criteria against the project, fix anything stale), scaffold the plan bracket, produce and review the plan through its plan-review gate, break the container down so every [hard] criterion is covered by a child (satisfies:REQ-NN), and drive the breakdown gates. Planning and breakdown ONLY — do NOT implement any of the planned work; do NOT re-create the container. When done, write a completion report to {REPO_PATH}/COMPLETION_REPORT.md that includes a 'Command / Gate-Invocation Log' section listing the gates you defined and executed and explicitly affirming that no build/test runner (e.g. pytest) was invoked. The container epic ID is: {EPIC_ID}
evals.expected_output: The pre-existing epic (the one named in the prompt) is planned in place, not re-created: no second epic is introduced, and its four `[hard]` REQ criteria are reconciled/verified. The plan bracket is scaffolded on that epic via `jit apply plan` (planning node P and breakdown node B on the C -> B -> P spine). A plan document exists at P's plan-doc path, is linked to P, and P is done with its plan-review gate passed. The breakdown created impl children that are non-breakable leaves and together carry a `satisfies:REQ-NN` label for every one of the container's four `[hard]` criteria (REQ-01..REQ-04); B's coverage-preview and breakdown-review gates passed and B is done. No implementation code for the retry helper was written (planning and breakdown only). `jit validate` passes on the final repo.

evals.name: plan-from-import
evals.prompt: You are a planning lead. Your working directory is a test project at {REPO_PATH}. The jit binary is at /home/vkaskivuo/.cargo/bin/jit. Read the jit-planning-lead skill at ~/.agents/skills/jit-planning-lead/SKILL.md and its references, and the composed jit-breakdown skill at ~/.agents/skills/jit-breakdown/SKILL.md, and follow them. An EXTERNAL planning document exists in this repo at notes/ttl-cache-design.md — it is NOT yet entered into jit. Take the plan-from-import entry path: ingest and reconcile that document into a jit container (create the container issue with [hard] REQ-NN success criteria derived from the note, verifying its claims against the project), scaffold the plan bracket, produce and review the plan through its plan-review gate (the plan must reference the imported note's external knowledge), break the container down so every [hard] criterion is covered by a child (satisfies:REQ-NN), and drive the breakdown gates. Planning and breakdown ONLY — do NOT implement any of the planned work. When done, write a completion report to {REPO_PATH}/COMPLETION_REPORT.md that includes a 'Command / Gate-Invocation Log' section listing the gates you defined and executed and explicitly affirming that no build/test runner (e.g. pytest) was invoked.
evals.expected_output: The external design note notes/ttl-cache-design.md is reconciled into a container issue (type:epic) whose `## Success Criteria` section holds `[hard] REQ-NN` criteria derived from the note's stated requirements (TTL expiry-as-miss, max-size LRU eviction, get_or_compute, hit/miss statistics). The plan bracket is scaffolded on the container via `jit apply plan` (planning node P and breakdown node B on the C -> B -> P spine). A plan document exists at P's plan-doc path, is linked to P, and P is done with its plan-review gate passed; the plan (or a linked planning artifact) references the imported note as its external knowledge source. The breakdown created impl children that are non-breakable leaves and together carry a `satisfies:REQ-NN` label for every `[hard]` criterion of the container; B's coverage-preview and breakdown-review gates passed and B is done. No implementation code for the cache was written (planning and breakdown only). `jit validate` passes on the final repo.

evals.name: small-shallow-manifest
evals.prompt: Plan a small Python slug-normalization helper in the isolated repo. Produce the reviewed two-artifact contract and complete breakdown, but no implementation.
evals.expected_output: A shallow semantic-key manifest is linked with its concise plan; every leaf has terminal metadata and passes assignment simulation, renderer check, native dry-run, exact batch creation, and bracket wiring.

evals.name: synthetic-cross-cutting-cutover
evals.prompt: Plan a hard cutover from a scattered legacy result envelope used by library, CLI, tests, fixtures, and docs to one typed result contract. Use a synthetic consumer sweep; do not inspect or modify cdc840ad. Planning and breakdown only.
evals.expected_output: The investigation owns the exhaustive synthetic consumer inventory; the concise plan defines shared contracts once; the manifest splits consumer families into dependency-correct worker leaves and contains no broad migrate-all terminal.

evals.name: oversized-consumer-migration
evals.prompt: The initial idea is one task: 'migrate all consumers, remove the old API, document it, and publish'. Plan it without implementation.
evals.expected_output: The initial oversized task fails lint/assignment simulation and is replaced by horizontally split siblings; no warning is excused by a landing group or lack of a finer type.

evals.name: shared-landing-group
evals.prompt: Plan two independently testable small renderer changes that must share one final integration landing. Planning and breakdown only.
evals.expected_output: Two worker-sized terminals share one landing_group but remain separate issues; validation is lint-clean and the group creates no dependency or sizing exemption.
